question.prompt: Let \(f(n) = n^3 - 5n^2 + 2n + 8,\) and let \(g(n) = n^3 - 6n^2 + 5n + 12.\) What is the sum of all integer values of \(n\) for which \(\dfrac{f(n)}{g(n)}\) is also an integer?

solutions.title: Factor and keep the exclusions
solutions.explanation:
Both cubics vanish at \(n=-1\), so they share the factor \(n+1\). Factoring will simplify the quotient and expose its integer-value condition.

Dividing by \(n+1\) and factoring the resulting quadratics gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(n)&=(n+1)(n^2-6n+8)\\
&=(n+1)(n-2)(n-4),\\
g(n)&=(n+1)(n^2-7n+12)\\
&=(n+1)(n-3)(n-4).
\end{aligned}
\]
The original denominator is zero at \(n=-1,3,4\), so all three values must be excluded, even if a factor later cancels.

For every allowed value,
\[
\frac{f(n)}{g(n)}
=\frac{n-2}{n-3}
=1+\frac{1}{n-3}.
\]
Since \(n-3\) is a nonzero integer, its reciprocal is an integer only when it is \(1\) or \(-1\). Equivalently, \(n-3\) must divide \(1\). Hence
\[
n-3=\pm1,
\qquad\text{giving}\qquad n=4\text{ or }n=2.
\]
The value \(4\) is excluded because \(g(4)=0\). The value \(2\) is allowed: \(f(2)=0\) and \(g(2)=6\), so the quotient is \(0\).

Thus the only eligible integer is \(2\), and the requested sum is \(\boxed{2}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
